notes: First page of the spotify site: a FULL page of 50 postings (so a next page is requested), 6 kept: workplaceType remote, hybrid (x3, two of them with two allLocations) and onsite. OWNERSHIP, EVIDENCE: TEXT_PARTIAL (no employer field in the payload; the posting text names the employer): 87 of the 90 postings on the board name Spotify somewhere (title, description, lists or closing text), 71 of them in the main description alone. The 3 that name it nowhere are the Ringer posting (1f56d4be-..., whose own text names The Ringer, a Spotify-owned podcast company) and two postings whose main description is empty (9f66e598-..., 9fd98cde-...), all three kept in these fixtures; the board is Spotify's by its URL (jobs.lever.co/spotify/<uuid>), not by those three. palantir was read once and 309 of 309 postings named Palantir, but that read is UNCAPTURED: no capture of it is committed, so treat that figure as unverified. The fixtures keep 6 of the 90, so the 87 cannot be re-derived from them. Documented (https://github.com/lever/postings-api): a public read API, HTTPS only, "Only published postings are public ... These jobs may be scraped by third parties"; the only documented rate limit is on application POSTs (not used). robots.txt of both api.lever.co and api.eu.lever.co: User-agent * / Allow: / / Crawl-delay: 1 - a longer gap than the 500 ms proposed in ats-config.ts. The payload carries NO employer name; employer evidence is the posting text naming the employer. Observed drift from the documentation: workplaceType is "onsite" on the live API, the README lists "on-site"; createdAt is present on every posting but is not in the README's field list. E-mail addresses and phone numbers inside string values were replaced by a parser; personal NAMES in free-text descriptions cannot be found by a parser and were not redacted (records were chosen with short descriptions to limit exposure).
